item.title: An empty bus pulled into Ridgland Farms in Wisconsin last week and emerged with more than 150 rescued beagles – who had never felt grass or fresh air in their lives. More than 2,000 beagles had been already rescued from the farm, a controversial biomedical research and breeding facility. CBS News' Adam Yamaguchi got to be there as the remaining dogs – many of them puppies – had their first taste of freedom. Many of the dogs were paralyzed with fear as they finally exited the cages they had been trapped in and entered the unknown world of caring human beings and safety. After protesters tried to break into the facility to rescue the dogs earlier this year, the facility decided to shut down its breeding operations. The remaining beagles were taken to Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Florida, where they will be put up for adoption. #beagles #rescue #dogrescue #dogs | CBS News

item.title: Florida teen Ishanvi Sabniveesu builds AI cane that describes surroundings, works offline and calls for help
item.description: Ishanvi Sabniveesu is the innovative mind behind CareCane, an AI-powered cane designed specifically for visually impaired individuals. This remarkable device not only helps users navigate obstacles but also enhances their environmental perception. With offline functionality for broader use and emergency assistance features, CareCane has garnered Sabniveesu second place at the prestigious Invention Convention U.S. Nationals. She is currently focused on introducing additional features and pursuing patent approval. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Mientras miramos hacia OpenAI y Anthropic, la auténtica revolución de la IA se está cocinando en otro lugar: SSI
item.description: Ilya Sutskever no es un científico especializado en inteligencia artificial (IA) más. Completó su formación en informática en el equipo que Geoffrey Hinton, premio Nobel de Física en 2024 y una de las figuras que ha hecho posible el aprendizaje profundo tal y como lo conocemos, lideraba en la Universidad de Toronto (Canadá). Junto a Hinton y Alex Krizhevsky desarrolló AlexNet, una red neuronal muy avanzada considerada unánimemente uno de los proyectos que han desencadenado la revolución actual de la IA . Entre 2013 y 2015 trabajó en Google Brain como investigador, y en 2015 abandonó Google… Fuente: Xataka.
